repo.name: ultratears
repo.description: Unofficial native PC and Steam Deck port of Tears of the Kingdom 1.4.3 using static recompilation. Builds locally from the player's own extracted game dump; no game files included.

releases.name: UltraTears 0.3.1
releases.body:
**An urgent performance update: higher frame rates and an even frame time.** - **Much smoother:** far fewer hitches when new parts of the world come into view; long frames are several times rarer. - **Faster:** roughly 35-40 % less GPU time per frame and roughly 40 % less CPU time spent recording the GPU's commands; the game's own code runs faster too. - **Lighter on the CPU:** fewer recording threads, so they no longer take cores from the game itself. - **Steam Deck: higher frame rate and a much more even frame time.** About a third less GPU time per frame, and the long hitches around busy places such as Lookout Landing are mostly gone. - Fixes: rare thread stalls, and terrain textures on slopes that crawled when the camera moved. **This is a big update:** the game is rebuilt almost from the start, about 30-40 minutes. Update when you are ready to wait that long; saves stay. Accept it in the launcher, or by hand: extract the new zip over your game folder (Steam Deck / Linux: replace `UltraTears.AppImage`; copied over from Windows, turn on **Allow executing file as program** in its Properties, **Permissions** tab, in Desktop Mode), start the launcher and click **Update the game**. **Known issues:** busy places like Lookout Landing are still limited by the CPU; rare flickering circles near Link. **Downloads** | File | For | |---|---| | `UltraTears-0.3.1-windows-x86_64.zip` (~150 MB) | Windows; it can also build the game for a Steam Deck | | `UltraTears.AppImage` (~210 MB) | Linux and the Steam Deck | Follow the [README](https://github.com/kuraeow/ultratears#readme) to install.
Full list of changes ## A faster and much smoother game This release is about speed and an even frame time, on the PC and on the Steam Deck alike. - **Far fewer render passes and less GPU work.** The game updates uniform buffers hundreds of times a frame in the middle of drawing; each update used to end the render pass, wait for all earlier GPU work and start the pass again. These updates now stay inside the pass: about two thirds fewer render passes and half the barriers, and roughly 35-40 % less GPU time per frame. - **Recording the GPU's commands takes much less CPU time** (roughly 40 % less): textures and buffers are bound in two sets and a draw's textures are not looked up again when they did not change, unchanged state is not recorded again, and fewer recording threads run, so they no longer take cores from the game itself (on a 16-thread CPU 4 instead of 8). - **The game's own code runs faster:** a few of its hottest functions, with jump tables the translator could not resolve, were built without optimisation; they are optimised now, with the slow path in a copy of their own. - **Far fewer hitches when new parts of the world come into view.** Several stalls happened on every burst of new textures: memory for uploads was given back to the driver and allocated again seconds later, every texture had a video memory allocation of its own, and new images and texture uploads held a lock that every other recording thread waited for. Upload memory is now kept for reuse, textures share large memory blocks, and images are made and textures prepared outside those locks. Frames over 60 ms dropped several times over. ## Steam Deck - **Higher frame rate and a much more even frame time.** The GPU time per frame fell by about a third, so the Deck is no longer held back by its GPU in busy places such as Lookout Landing, and the long hitches when running in and out of such places (up to a second when many new textures arrived at once) are mostly gone. - On the Deck's four cores, the fewer recording threads leave more of the CPU to the game. ## Fixes - Waiting on several objects: a pending cancel is now kept for the next wait that would block, and a signal that wakes all waiters changes the value as the console does. Both could stall game threads in rare cases. - Shader translator: the gradients of texture lookups with explicit derivatives are read per coordinate, so terrain on slopes picks the right mip level instead of a too sharp one that crawled when the camera moved. ## For testers - The log's "long submission" line now says where a long frame's recording went (waiting for the GPU, new images, uploads, memory made, the uniform snapshot), and the frame interval line counts frames over 25 ms. ## Known issues - Busy places such as Lookout Landing are still limited by the CPU, the game's own work and the recording of the GPU's commands; the next versions keep working on it. - Rarely, white or red circles flicker at some distance from Link; not understood yet.
UltraTears is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. You need your own legally obtained copy of the game.

releases.name: UltraTears 0.3.0
releases.body:
- **Steam Deck / AMD: the Depths are fixed.** The ground, the cave walls and Link's lighting are back. - **Gyro aiming:** no more drift, and it now works on the Steam Deck too, with your Steam Input layout untouched. - **Faster:** the game's code runs faster (registers kept in host registers), better thread scheduling, faster loading, no pause when saving, fewer GPU stalls; roughly 10-15 % more fps in busy places. - **AMD:** flickering fog fixed by shader translator fixes. - Launcher: updates are checked at every start. **This is a big update:** the game is rebuilt almost from the start, about 30-40 minutes. Update when you are ready to wait that long; saves stay. Accept it in the launcher (0.2.0's launcher checks once a day), or by hand: extract the new zip over your game folder (Steam Deck / Linux: replace `UltraTears.AppImage`; copied over from Windows, turn on **Allow executing file as program** in its Properties, **Permissions** tab, in Desktop Mode), start the launcher and click **Update the game**. **Known issues:** busy places like Lookout Landing are still slower than the rest of the game; rare flickering circles near Link. **Downloads** | File | For | |---|---| | `UltraTears-0.3.0-windows-x86_64.zip` (~150 MB) | Windows; it can also build the game for a Steam Deck | | `UltraTears.AppImage` (~210 MB) | Linux and the Steam Deck | Follow the [README](https://github.com/kuraeow/ultratears#readme) to install.
Full list of changes ## Steam Deck and AMD graphics - **The Depths draw properly on AMD** (Steam Deck, Radeon on Linux, the Windows build under Proton): the ground and the cave walls were missing and Link was dark. The terrain's patch tables were bound as if they were a 64 KiB uniform buffer wherever the graphics driver's uniform and storage alignments are the same, which is the case on AMD and Mesa. - **Flickering fog on AMD:** the shader translator now gives Maxwell's results where Vulkan leaves a result undefined (bit fields past bit 31, local variables read before they are written), and three more fixes: the vertex position is invariant across the passes that draw the same geometry, the depth compared against a 16-bit shadow map is rounded to 16 bits as on the Switch, and unwritten vertex outputs start at (0, 0, 0, 1). - **Gyro aiming on the Steam Deck:** the Deck's own gyro is read from its controller while buttons and sticks keep coming through Steam Input, so your Steam layout stays as it is. Nothing to set up. - Fewer GPU stalls: render passes no longer wait for all earlier GPU work, and image layouts change only when they must (in the Depths about 30 % fewer barriers a frame and nearly 90 % fewer layout changes). AMD drivers pay for these more than NVIDIA's. ## Speed and smoothness - **The game's code runs faster:** inside a function the Switch CPU's registers and flags now live in C local variables, so the compiler keeps them in host registers. Checked against the previous translation on 1000 game functions from the same random states: no difference. - About 630 functions (459 of them in the SDK) were built without optimisation by mistake; they are optimised now. - Thread scheduling: a higher-priority thread now takes a virtual core at system calls and indirect calls instead of waiting for the holder to sleep; Windows uses SRW locks and condition variables; short sleeps are exact; 848 busy-wait loops of the game give their core to a waiting thread after 50 microseconds. - Loading: the game's zstd-compressed files decode with the system's libzstd, several times faster; saving writes to the disk on a thread of its own, so the game no longer stops for 95-135 ms on each save. - Command recording: the uniform-buffer capture at each submission no longer compares every range with every pending GPU write; recording threads keep the memory pool they used last. In busy places such as Lookout Landing that is roughly 10-15 % more frames a second. - Smaller things: memory barriers without a full fence where the game asks for a one-sided one, a clock without 128-bit divisions, fewer reallocations while recording, environment lookups cached on Linux too, the render pass kept when the game sets the same targets again. ## Fixes - **Gyro aiming drift** (aim creeping to one side and then the other with the controller still): the gyro's zero-rate bias is now measured from your own controller whenever it is still, in the first seconds, and taken off; the tilt correction uses the gravity your controller actually reads. Samples are timed by the sensor. - After StartSixAxisSensor the gyro no longer hands out samples from before it. - Equipment could stay locked for a moment after loading a save at real-time frame steps. - Cube-map flags are set only on cube textures and arrays drawn to, not on every square texture array (on AMD this changed the ground textures' layout); depth sampled without a comparison reads one texel, as on the Switch. ## Launcher - Updates are checked at every start, in the background; with no answer from GitHub nothing is shown. - Pre-releases are not offered as updates. - An update with the same version number is still offered as an update. - The game language's default reads "As in the system". ## Known issues - Busy places such as Lookout Landing are still slower than the rest of the game: the game's own work and the recording of the GPU's commands take about the same time each frame. This is what the next version works on. - Rarely, white or red circles flicker at some distance from Link; not understood yet.
UltraTears is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. You need your own legally obtained copy of the game.

releases.name: UltraTears 0.2.0
releases.body:
**UltraTears 0.2.0** builds a native PC version of *Tears of the Kingdom* 1.4.3 from your own dumped copy, on your PC. No game files, keys or Nintendo code are included. - **A launcher instead of the console:** choose your game folder, click **Prepare the game**, then **Play**. Settings, updates and a full rebuild are in the same window. - **Steam Deck and Linux (experimental):** a native build, made on the Deck from the AppImage or on your Windows PC. Starts from Steam in Gaming Mode. - **60 fps** at the proper game speed, with even frame pacing (up to 240 as a beta). - **Any resolution and screen shape**, FSR 1 scene scaling and sharpening, an FPS counter. - **No shader stutter:** every shader is compiled for your graphics card while the game is prepared. - **AMD:** the black screen on Windows is fixed; a possible fix for flickering fog. - **The Depths** draw properly on Windows, and the crash after the bats at the start of the game is fixed. - Faster texture loading, less memory, smaller downloads, CPUs without AVX2 supported. **Updating from 0.1.0:** extract the new zip over your old folder (saves stay) and start `UltraTears Launcher.exe`. **Known issues:** on the Steam Deck the Depths' ground is missing and the frame rate drops in busy places; some cloth tears; the mouse does not move the camera yet. **Downloads** | File | For | |---|---| | `UltraTears-0.2.0-windows-x86_64.zip` (~150 MB) | Windows; it can also build the game for a Steam Deck | | `UltraTears.AppImage` (~210 MB) | Linux and the Steam Deck | Follow the [README](https://github.com/kuraeow/ultratears#readme) to install.
Full list of changes ## The launcher (new) - **`UltraTears Launcher.exe` replaces `setup.bat` and the console window.** Choose the folder with your `exefs` and `romfs` (or drop it onto the window) and the launcher checks right away that it is version 1.4.3, and says why if it is not. One click prepares the game: an overall progress bar, every step with the time it took and the time left, a hardware check before the long part, and on an error a button that opens the log. Then: **Play**. - If the build stops or the PC turns off, **Continue preparing** picks up where it stopped. The game can be installed into another folder than the one you extracted. - **Updates:** once a day the launcher checks for a new release and offers it. It downloads it, verifies its size and SHA-256, puts it in place (your data and saves stay) and rebuilds only what changed. `updates=off` in `ultratears-launcher.ini` turns this off. - **Game settings on the Play screen:** window mode, resolution, scene scale, sharpness, frame limit, V-Sync and the FPS counter. A Language tab for the launcher and the game's text, and a Debug tab: Debug mode for performance reports, F9 snapshots, GPU markers for crash reports, and a full rebuild. - English and Russian, scaled to the screen (larger on a Steam Deck), usable with a controller. - A new icon for the game and the launcher: the emblem from the cover. - Windows SmartScreen may warn about the launcher because it is not signed: **More info → Run anyway**. ## Steam Deck and Linux (new, experimental) - **A native Linux build** (not Proton), two ways to the same game folder: - on your Windows PC: choose **For Linux (Steam Deck)** or **Both platforms** in the launcher. You get `UltraTears-SteamDeck.tar` (~27 GB) to copy to the Deck and extract; - on the Deck itself: download the AppImage, allow it to run, start it and prepare the game there. - **One program:** `UltraTears.AppImage` in the game folder opens the launcher; with `--play` in Steam's launch options it starts the game directly. It starts from Steam in Gaming Mode (a patched AppImage runtime: under Steam it could not find `fusermount` and quit at once). - **Graphics prepared for the Deck's own GPU:** the first **Play** on the Deck compiles every shader with its driver (about 2 minutes, with a progress bar, once), so the game itself has no shader stalls. - **Updates:** the launcher finds a new release itself, or put the new `UltraTears.AppImage` into the game folder in place of the old one (it has the same name), and the launcher offers to update the game. The tools come from the AppImage itself: the game folder keeps no second copy of them. - In Gaming Mode the launcher has its own folder picker that works with the controller. - The Deck's defaults: fullscreen 1280×800 (16:10, with the interface laid out for it), 40 fps. - The windows have the UltraTears icon, and the launcher writes `ultratears-launcher.log` beside the game. - Needs SteamOS 3.7 or Linux 6.7+ with glibc 2.34+. On an older kernel the launcher warns that the game will be slow. - The Linux base comes from **crazyquark**'s PR #42, on top of **triadwoozie**'s Linux work: thank you both. ## 60 fps - **The game runs at 60 fps** (30 on the Switch), at its proper speed. The limit is set in the launcher: 30, 40, 45 or 60 (the default); as a beta also 120, 144, the monitor's refresh rate, or up to 240. Measured in the Depths: game time keeps up with real time within 1 % at every limit, and Link runs and walks at the same speed. - **Even frame pacing:** every frame is shown on its own slot (every 16.7 ms at 60), not as soon as it is drawn, and the game moves by the time between those slots. - The game never steps by less than 1/240 s: with shorter steps its physics runs out of memory or crashes on some saves (found by totk-pc-recomp on 240–280 Hz monitors). - The weapon, shield and material quick menus show the blurred world behind them again instead of black. - Above ~63 fps the game itself has known problems no port has fixed yet: the camera turns too fast and Link does not climb steps. That is why everything above 60 is a beta. - The game-code patches for this follow **MacNativeGames**' (MIT), and the frame pacing and the quick menus follow **totk-pc-recomp**'s (MIT). ## Resolution and image - **Any output resolution**, from 1280×720 to 4K or the screen's own, with the menus and HUD drawn at that size. Wide and tall screens too: 16:10, 21:9 and 32:9, with the camera and the interface laid out for them. - **Scene scale** separately from the output, with FSR 1 modes: Performance (50 %), Balanced (59 %), Quality (67 %), Ultra quality (77 %), the game's own 83 %, none (100 %), and supersampling at 150 % and 200 %. - **Sharpness** (FSR 1 RCAS): off, 25, 50 (default), 75 or 100 %. - **FPS counter**: F10 in the game, or the launcher's setting. - Grass is drawn much further away. ## Graphics fixes - **AMD on Windows: the black screen is fixed** (#2, #16, #23; confirmed on a Radeon 610M, #31). Thanks to **Moran45** for the idea and a first test on a Radeon 780M (PR #36). - **AMD and the Steam Deck: possible fix for flickering fog.** AMD's drivers cannot do a depth comparison some of the game's effects rely on; such textures now go through a depth copy, as totk-pc-recomp does. Not confirmed yet: if fog still flickers on your AMD card, please report it. - AMD RDNA2: no more "device lost" at the logo. AMD and Intel: shadow edges without dashed lines. - **The Depths:** the ground is drawn everywhere, with its proper textures, and Link is lit next to it; the Depths map opens. Thanks to **valentderah** (totk-pc-recomp), whose notes had the colour order of the textures involved. - The ground no longer tears into huge wedges across the screen, and animated objects no longer tear into wedges. - Fixed the giant "green planes" on the Great Sky Island, the black minimap, and dark squares of ground without grass. - Shadows: the dark "box" on the ground in front of Link is gone (#34). Thanks to **A-FadedAway**, who found the cause. - Effects that use noise textures the game makes on the GPU have them now (they were empty). ## Crashes and hangs - Fixed the crash in the cutscene after the bats at the start of the game (#4). Thanks to **ardmeteor999**, **passballtotucker**, **ScrubOasis** and **Douglasgabrielc** for the reports. - Fixed the stop with "no function at 8006eb850" when loading a save or later in play (#18). Thanks to **PashaKagan**, who found the same cause and sent the same fix (PR #24). - Fixed a GPU hang ("device lost") every few minutes. - Fixed shaders the NVIDIA driver crashed on. - Running out of video memory no longer ends the game at once, and when memory really runs out, a message says so. - A graphics card that cannot run the game (Intel HD 600, Iris Xe and others) gets a clear message instead of a crash (#17, #26). ## Performance - **No stutter from shader compilation.** Every shader is compiled with your graphics driver while the game is prepared (the "Preparing the graphics" step), and again before **Play** only after a driver update. A driver that crashes on a shader no longer stops this: the rest is compiled, and that one later. - The game's draw commands are recorded on several threads, so the CPU side of a frame is much shorter. - Fewer frame drops while the world loads: texture loading is 4–10 times faster, and the game no longer waits for the whole GPU queue when it frees memory. - Less memory: about 6.8 GB allocated instead of 8.3, about 4.8 GB of RAM instead of 6.3 in the same place. - On CPUs without AVX2, fused multiply-add is now rounded exactly as on the Switch (from totk-pc-recomp). ## The builder - **Smaller downloads:** the Windows package and the AppImage carry only the parts of the tools the build uses. - **CPUs without AVX2** (Intel Core 2nd/3rd generation, AMD FX) are supported: the game is built for them, a little slower (#19). - The graphics card is checked before the build, naming what is missing, instead of failing at the first start. - A RomFS that is not 1.4.3's: the error now names the folders that differ, so you can tell a missing update from mods or a damaged copy. - The translated shaders are one file instead of ~143,000 (#22; thanks to **PashaKagan**, who proposed the same in PR #25). The shader step no longer reports 82 failed shaders (#37; thanks to **Atterax**). - The build uses much less memory, no longer fails without Git installed (#29), shows progress for every step, and resumes broken downloads, switching to a mirror when a host is blocked. - **Building from source** is one command (`python tools/setup.py --dump `) and gives the same game folder as a release, launcher included ([BUILDING.md](https://github.com/kuraeow/ultratears/blob/main/BUILDING.md)). ## Controls - A stick dead zone: Link no longer walks on his own with a worn stick (#39). - Gyro: the controller's drift at rest is taken off, so aiming no longer creeps (#39). ## Logs and reports - The game always writes `ultratears.log` beside it (the previous run's as `ultratears-previous.log`). Attach it to a report. - For performance reports, turn on Debug mode in the launcher's Debug tab: the log then has frame timing and memory. ## Known issues - **Steam Deck:** in the Depths the ground is missing and Link's lighting is wrong (fine on Windows); frame rate drops below 40 in busy places. Both are being worked on. - Some cloth and banners tear (for example at a tower and a stable). - Where frames are heavy (the Depths, big fights), the rate can drop below 60. - The mouse does not move the camera yet: use a controller or the keyboard.
UltraTears is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. You need your own legally obtained copy of the game.

releases.name: UltraTears 0.1.0-beta
releases.body:
First public build. You need your own copy of The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
with update 1.4.3 (exefs and romfs extracted from your console).

1. Download UltraTears-builder-0.1.0-windows-x86_64.zip and unzip it.
2. Put exefs and romfs into game\.
3. Run setup.bat (about 30 minutes, once).
4. Start UltraTears.exe.

Contains no game data. Not affiliated with Nintendo. See README for details.
